originalTitle: Rachika Nayar’s Heaven Come Crashing is an instrumental epic of desperate longing

content: Two minutes and thirty seconds into the title track of Rachika Nayar’s Heaven Come Crashing, an absolutely massive drum and bass beat drops. As a fan of Nayar’s debut record Our Hands Against The Dusk, it caught me off guard. That album has no percussion on it at all. Heaven Comes Crashing is almost entirely drum-free, too. There are some rapid-fire mechanical hi-hats on the second track, “Tetramorph,” and the back half of track six, “Gayatri,” has what sounds like a snare buried deep in the mix. But it isn’t until track seven that Nayar delivers an unexpected drum explosion, before immediately retreating to the soothing wash of “Sleepless,” just one song later.  [Media: https://rachika.bandcamp.com/album/heaven-come-crashing] Nayar’s unique brand of guitar-heavy ambient-adjacent music plays almost like a version of M83 from an alternate universe. One where instead of turning to ‘80s pop music for inspiration, Anthony Gonzalez mined his instrumental epics for every last drop of emotion. Heaven Comes Crashing is as emotionally heavy as the title would imply but uses surprisingly few words to get there. The only vocals come courtesy of Maria BC, who floats over the title track and the stunning album closer “Our Wretched Fate,” where she worldlessly belts out her laments. There are lyrics on “Heaven Comes Crashing,” but they’re almost indecipherable as Maria BC whispers beneath an ocean of flailing guitar lines and sparkling drones: > Is it morning? > I don’t remember going to sleep > How can we face the day > Like this? > You throw down your arms and count to see > How deep it is Instead of words, Nayar turns to heavily processed guitar, lonesome textures, and the occasional burst of trance chords to capture the desperate longing at the album’s core. But the album is also an indictment of the sort of abandon that often accompanies unbridled passion. It’s bookended by “Our Wretched Fantasy” and “Our Wretched Fate,” betraying a certain disgust for its own emotional recklessness. Track three isn’t “Death and Love”; it’s “Death and Limerence” — opting to spotlight unhealthy romantic obsession rather than fulfilling emotional partnership, through U2-esque guitar lines that eventually drown beneath heavily reverbed and out-of-tune tremolo-picked notes. That’s followed by the unease of “Nausea,” which builds from an unsteady drone to maximalist panic of ‘90s synths and one of the simplest and prettiest guitar melodies on the record. The ambient emo of “Promises” follows, leading into “Gayatri,” which ratchets up the energy and serves as a bridge to the explosive title track. Rachika Nayar’s Heaven Comes Crashing is available on Bandcamp and most major streaming services, including Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music, Qobuz, and Deezer.

chineseContent: Rachika Nayar 的 Heaven Come Crashing 的主打歌开始两分三十秒后，出现了绝对巨大的鼓和贝斯节奏。作为纳亚尔首张唱片《我们的手对抗黄昏》的粉丝，这让我措手不及。那张专辑根本没有打击乐。 Heaven Comes Crashing 也几乎完全没有鼓。第二首曲目“Tetramorph”中有一些快速的机械踩镲，第六首曲目“Gayatri”的后半部分听起来像是深埋在混音中的军鼓。但直到第七首，纳亚尔才发出了意想不到的鼓点爆炸声，然后立即退回到舒缓的“Sleepless”中，仅仅一首歌之后。  [媒体：https://rachika.bandcamp.com/album/heaven-come-crashing] Nayar 独特的吉他重环境邻近音乐品牌演奏起来几乎就像来自另一个宇宙的 M83 版本。安东尼·冈萨雷斯没有从 80 年代的流行音乐中寻找灵感，而是从他的器乐史诗中挖掘每一滴情感。正如标题所暗示的那样，《天堂来了》的情感沉重，但令人惊讶的是，它只用了很少的文字就达到了这一点。唯一的声音来自 Maria BC，她飘浮在主打歌和令人惊叹的专辑结尾曲《Our Wretched Fate》中，她在其中无情地高声唱出她的哀歌。 《Heaven Comes Crashing》中有歌词，但歌词几乎难以辨认，因为 Maria BC 在一片挥舞着的吉他线和闪闪发光的嗡嗡声的海洋下低声说：> 现在是早上吗？ > 我不记得要睡觉 > 我们该如何面对这一天 > 像这样？ > 你放下双臂，数数看看有多深 > Nayar 没有使用言语，而是用经过精心处理的吉他、孤独的纹理以及偶尔爆发的 trance 和弦来捕捉专辑核心的绝望渴望。但专辑是
